attributes.body_ja:
「ところで」は、名詞（めいし）の「ところ」と格助詞（かくじょし）の「で」からできた接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）です。新（あたら）しい話題（わだい）を出（だ）して、会話（かいわ）の流（なが）れを変（か）えるときに使（つか）います。

「ところで」は、主（おも）に、それまでの話（はなし）とは別（べつ）の話題（わだい）や質問（しつもん）を始（はじ）めるときに、文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）で使（つか）います。

「ところで」には、それまで話（はな）していたことから、話（はな）し手（て）が突然（とつぜん）別（べつ）のことを思（おも）い出（だ）して、新（あたら）しい話題（わだい）に変（か）えるようなニュアンスがあります。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「ところで」が動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）のあとに付（つ）くと、全（まった）く別（べつ）の意味（いみ）になります。この「たところで」は、「もし (A) をしても意味（いみ）がない」を意味（いみ）します。これは上級（じょうきゅう）の文法（ぶんぽう）なので、またあとで学（まな）びましょう。
attributes.body:
ところで is a conjunction particle that is made up of the noun, ところ 'place', and the case marking particle で. It is used in a similar way to 'by the way', or 'incidentally' in English, but will only be used for introducing new topics, not continuing within the same topic.

ところで will primarily appear at the beginning of a sentence, before making a statement or asking a question about something unrelated.

The literal translation of ところで is closer to 'and with that', and implies that something (within the previous topic) suddenly reminded the speaker of another thing (that happens to be a new topic).

Caution

When ところで appears after the past tense of a verb as たところで, it carries a different meaning, and will express that something isn't the case, despite (A). This is an advanced grammar point that will be covered at another stage.

attributes.description: What's the difference between ところで and ちなみに ?

attributes.body: Both can be used to shift the topic, but といえば is used after a noun to bring up something related or comment on that thing, e.g. 京都といえば、有名なお寺が多いね ('Speaking of Kyoto, there many famous temples, aren't there.'). In contrast, ところで typically starts a new sentence to introduce an unrelated topic, e.g. ところで、週末の予定は？ ('By the way, what are your plans for the weekend?').

first_relatable.title: といえば
first_relatable.meaning: Speaking of, If it were the case that

attributes.body: Both can be used at the beginning of a sentence to introduce a new topic, but with different nuance. ところで marks a clear, unrelated shift, similar to 'by the way' in English, e.g. ところで、週末は何してた？ ('By the way, what did you do this weekend?') そういえば recalls something related to the current topic, e.g. そういえば、田中さんに会ったよ ('Speaking of which, I saw Tanaka.')
